newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas firms with stock demand, maintenance.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas firms with stock demand, maintenance.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were steady to higher Tuesday despite forecasts for cooler weather later this week and Hurricane Hortense's turn away from the Gulf Coast, industry sources said.
Sources attributed the firmness to a high storage demand and ongoing maintenance.

Swing prices on the U.S. Gulf Coast pipes remained strong in the $1.76-1.81 per million British thermal units range, helped in part by news that there was a leak on Columbia Gas's northern Virginia line, resulting in lost production of about 350 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd).
The impact was short-lived, however, since the pipeline was expected to return to service today.
Extensive maintenance on El Paso and Transwestern coupled with continued heat in Texas and California supported the Permian basin market today.
Traders reported closing most deals in the high-$1.50s to mid-$1.60s, with the higher prices evident in late trading.
El Paso's Chaco plant in New Mexico is expected to be down until Thursday for maintenance, affecting about 300-500 mmcfd of supply.

Additional maintenance is underway downstream in New Mexico. At the Belen station, beginning tomorrow and ending Sunday, about 70 mmcfd of supply will be off the market. Meanwhile at the Roswell station, a one-day maintenance outage is affecting about 150 mmcfd today.

Prices were similarly higher at the southern California border where traders reported closing most deals in the mid-$1.70s. At Waha, the nine to 10 cent premium to the Permian market was constant as gas sold at the west Texas hub in the high-$1.60s to mid-$1.70s.

In the Midcontinent, prices rose by more than five cents today into the mid-$1.60s early to the low-$1.70s late. Sources attributed the strengthening to a strong storage buying interest and the maintenance on El Paso and Transwestern.
At 1100 EDT, Hortense was over the eastern Dominican Republic and moving at 12 miles per hour in a west-northwest path.
